clue.text: Decide to gamble no further on finding money in the food

definitions.meaning: a gambler exchanging tokens for money at the end of play, so quitting
a whimsical literal reading: cash discovered inside your plate of fried potatoes

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read twice: the idiom for quitting a game, and literally as cash turning up in one's chips, i.e. fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers swap their tokens for cash when they stop playing, hence the idiom for quitting.

clue.text: Rash to dip me in ice stupidly

indicators.note: acting stupidly suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that dunking them in ice would be a foolish, rash thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges DIPME and ICE; 'in' merely joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash of something is a sudden widespread outbreak, which is what an epidemic is.

clue.text: Examination raising some regular objections

indicators.note: raising says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An examination that keeps provoking the same complaints from candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raising' reads upwards: LARO, inside 'reguLAR Objections', becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva or language exam, is called an oral.

clue.text: Uninformed soldier turning to girl with book

indicators.note: turning means the word for the soldier is flipped round

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Nora is a girl's name
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A soldier who knows nothing goes to a girl holding a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' flips GI to IG; 'to' and 'with' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninformed lacks knowledge, the core meaning of ignorant.

clue.text: Left possessions in landed property

definitions.meaning: everything a person owns that is passed on at death
a large area of land with a country house

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' merely joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's assets form their estate, and a large rural landholding is also called one.

clue.text: Ismail features in French sea song

parts.note: mer is French for sea
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A man named Ismail stars in a French sea shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ismail' is the definition: Ismail Merchant, the film producer of Merchant Ivory, who made feature films.
explanation.definitionFit: Ismail Merchant was the Indian-born producer of the Merchant Ivory films, so the surname goes with the first name.

clue.text: Isle that's lying about northeast

indicators.note: the word for that is lying round the outside of the compass point, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written, the 's being 'is'
NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies about an island off the northeast.
explanation.walkthrough: THANET is in the far east of Kent, England, once separated from the mainland. 'lying about' signals the enclosure, and the 's of 'that's' is simply 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is the north-eastern tip of Kent, once separated from the mainland by a channel.

clue.text: More grand screen characters seen at the Victorian place of entertainment

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are treated as loose characters to be reassembled

explanation.surface: Bigger film stars turn up at an old Victorian pleasure venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen characters' looks like film actors, but 'characters' signals that the fifteen letters of MORE GRAND SCREEN are rearranged. CREMORNE GARDENS were pleasure gardens in Chelsea, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremorne Gardens in Chelsea were popular nineteenth-century pleasure gardens with music, dancing and fireworks.

clue.text: How father put sugar over the vegetable shoots?

parts.note: as can mean how, in the sense of 'in the manner that'
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: turned over, so the word sugar is read backwards

explanation.surface: A question about how Dad sprinkled sugar over the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SUGAR into RAGUS; 'put' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is eaten as its young tender spears, which are the plant's shoots.

clue.text: Liquid used in some thermometers

indicators.note: the answer is used in, i.e. sits inside, the following words

explanation.surface: A fluid found in certain thermometers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'somE' into 'THERmometers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a volatile liquid once widely used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman's secret goal, perhaps

parts.note: hid means kept secret

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word goal may come in another form, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman has a hidden ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GOAL to ALGO; the 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the minor Spanish nobility, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: Mystery of cuckoopint found outside container

indicators.note: one word is found outside the other, enclosing it

parts.note: the cuckoopint, or lords-and-ladies, is a wild arum
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A botanical puzzle concerning a wild flower seen outside a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoopint, also called lords-and-ladies, is a wild arum; 'found outside' signals the enclosure and 'of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcanum is a secret or mystery, especially one known only to initiates.

clue.text: Recalled Oriental island's fame

indicators.note: called back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: E for East, as in Oriental
the Isle of Man, a crossword staple, gives MAN

explanation.surface: Someone remembers how famous an Eastern island once was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses E + MAN, EMAN, as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a name for oneself is to win fame, so name means renown.

clue.text: Masculine element taken into account by criminal

parts.note: male means masculine
a factor is an element considered in a decision

explanation.surface: Gender is weighed up when a court considers an offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits a crime.

clue.text: Embrace the French model with throat-band

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
le is French for the
the Model T Ford gives T

explanation.surface: A French model embraces someone wearing a choker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is a close-fitting ornament worn round the neck, a band at the throat.

clue.text: Inexperienced seafarer comes ashore on island

parts.note: a ship lands when it comes ashore
the Isle of Man gives MAN

explanation.surface: A novice sailor finally steps ashore on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just links, in a down clue placing one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In naval usage a landsman was a sailor on his first voyage, lacking sea experience.

clue.text: Object to something in the paper …

definitions.meaning: a piece of writing printed in a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the two definitions; the surface suggests protesting against a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is both a thing and a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Drink a Conservative takes, depending on chance

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Whether a Tory politician has a pint is a matter of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory, from Latin alea 'dice', describes something governed by luck.

clue.text: Crazy person may be expert on drug

parts.note: a crack shot is an expert one, so crack means skilled
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone deranged may be an authority on narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' and 'on' are links; 'on' puts the expert above the drug in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or mad person with bizarre ideas.

clue.text: … about French town sign for theological colleges

indicators.note: turned about, so the town's name is read backwards

parts.note: Nimes is a town in southern France
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a newspaper piece on a French town's star sign and its seminaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NIMES to SEMIN. The ellipsis carries the sentence on from 17-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminaries are colleges training people for the priesthood or ministry.

clue.text: Mother to get granny one tomorrow

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
nan is a British word for grandmother
a means one

explanation.surface: Mother is to fetch Granny one tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Manana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English for an indefinite later time.

clue.text: Sails with the top people

definitions.meaning: a royal is a small sail set high on a mast above the topgallant
members of a royal family, the highest in the land

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Royals are both high square sails and members of a monarch's family.

clue.text: It's a long story about a thing without substance

indicators.note: turned about, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a gas has no fixed form or substance

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a lengthy tale about something insubstantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A + GAS round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Integrity shown in bed, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a garden plant that might be growing in a flower bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'shown' links. Honesty (Lunaria) is a garden plant with silvery seed pods; 'bed' is a flower bed, not a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The virtue of honesty and the plant honesty share the name, the plant being grown in garden beds.

clue.text: When one man came in, another was grateful

indicators.note: one name came in, i.e. entered, the other

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, the other man
Hank is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone was thankful when one man walked in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one man entering a room; 'came in' really signals one name going inside another, and 'When' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To express being grateful to someone is to give them thanks.

clue.text: In these days we may be stricken with fear

indicators.note: we are placed in the abbreviation for these days

parts.note: AD, anno domini, the present era

explanation.surface: Modern times may leave us feeling frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In these days' reads as one phrase, but 'In' is the insertion signal and 'these days' gives the abbreviation for anno domini; 'may be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Awed means filled with awe, an overwhelming mix of fear and wonder.

clue.text: Milk drunk in Columbus's ship?

definitions.meaning: a British informal word for a pint of milk
one of the three ships on Columbus's 1492 voyage

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two definitions. PINTA is British slang for a pint of milk, once delivered to doorsteps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinta is both a doorstep pint of milk and the name of one of Columbus's caravels.

clue.text: Elgar work won't upset Darlington, for example

indicators.note: work as a command to rework the letters, used as a sign to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A music piece by Elgar will not upset a town in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' and 'upset' both suggest rearranging ELGAR and WONT. Darlington is a town in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a sizeable town in north-east England, an example of a large town.
